Hi all — triage update:

What we see:
- Tempest2B serving pool in us-west-2 experienced a CPU/KV cache saturation event starting ~07:48 PT.
- Error surface: majority are 503s with "model_unavailable" returned by the runtime; a minority are downstream timeout cascades.
- No config changes or deployments in the window.

Immediate mitigations applied (08:35 PT):
1) Increased Tempest2B autoscale max by 30% for us-west-2 to drain backlog.
2) Enabled fallback routing: new traffic from AtlasAI is routed to Tempest2B-quantized (compat) where applicable.
3) Short-term prefix cache warmup enabled for AtlasAI project to reduce KV pressure.

Impact: 503 rate dropped from ~17% to ~2.5% within 10 minutes after actions; latency for routed requests improved. We're monitoring for regression.

Next steps:
- Collect full request traces and heap/KV metrics (uploading to ticket).
- If instability persists, we'll shift heavier batch jobs to alternative model families for 1-2 hours.

I'll post the incident ticket and logs here in 15 minutes.

-Ben
Ben Carter
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference

Attachments referenced: upload to RW-INC-4821 (request traces, heap dumps).

Hi Andrew —

Quick customer-facing summary of what's happening and what we did:

Summary: We observed an elevated rate of 503 errors affecting Tempest2B in us-west-2 starting ~07:48 PT. Our team identified KV cache saturation in the serving runtime as the proximate cause.

What we did:
- Scaled Tempest2B serving pool to increase capacity.
- Temporarily routed new AtlasAI traffic to a quantized Tempest2B variant where compatible to reduce pressure.
- Enabled targeted cache warmup for your project to reduce cold-KV misses.

Result: 503 rate dropped to ~2-3% and latency is back within your SLO for interactive sessions. We are still watching batch scoring jobs and will proactively throttle large background jobs if we see re-escalation.

Compensation: We will apply a one-time 10% service credit for the impacted day to your account DA-9072 while we complete the post-incident review.

Follow-ups: Ben will share the internal incident link and a timeline; we will send a short postmortem within 72 hours with root cause, longer-term mitigations, and action items.

If you prefer, we can schedule a 30-minute bridge to walk through the technical details.

Thanks again for flagging this quickly — we'll keep you updated.

Best,

Subject: Tempest2B incident — recovery confirmed and postmortem link

Hi Andrew and team — final update from ops:

Status: The Tempest2B serving cluster has been stable for 4+ hours (since ~09:00 PT) with error rates <0.5% and latencies within baseline. We have rolled back the temporary autoscale cap and kept the cache warmup policy for your project for 24 hours as a precaution.

Root cause (summary): Rapid KV cache churn caused by a combination of increased small-batch scoring traffic and a pathological sequence-length distribution that triggered inefficient kernel paths in one of our nodes. The node-level memory pressure produced transient failures which surfaced as 503s.

Longer-term fixes in progress:
- Improve KV eviction policy and early-warning metrics for cache pressure.
- Add model-serving route diversification so single-node pathologies don't correlate across the pool.
- Optimize the kernel selection heuristics for short sequence, high-QPS patterns.

Documents: Postmortem & timeline: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/RW-INC-4821 (will be updated with full analysis). PagerDuty incident: https://redwood.pagerduty.com/incidents/PDT-8342

If you want the raw traces or a short technical bridge, ping me and we'll schedule. Apologies again for the disruption — thank you for your patience and for the quick report.

-Ben
Ben Carter
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference
